result.authors: ['Mira K. Deshpande', ' Julian P. Alvarez', ' Hana Sato']
result.journal: ACM Transactions on Autonomous and Adaptive Systems
result.keywords: We study an adaptive learning framework for distributed episodic decision-making in heterogeneous nonlinear systems with continuous state-action spaces. The method combines metric-space discretization with iterative update rules to coordinate multiple agents under partial information and time-varying dynamics. A data-driven partitioning scheme refines regions that are frequently visited or yield strong returns, while a consensus-style control layer propagates shared value estimates across agents. We provide finite-sample performance guarantees and show that the approach retains robustness without requiring a precomputed discretization or a simulator. Experiments on synthetic multi-agent benchmarks demonstrate improved tracking and reward maximization relative to uniform discretization and standard iterative learning baselines.
result.title: Adaptive Discretization and Iterative Control for Distributed Episodic Learning in Nonlinear Metric Systems
